needs_human.note: The spec does not state that a thumbnail download publishes atomically. Section 5 says only that failure handling is unchanged. The code publishes through `generating_file` (service.py:545-546), and the tests attribute 'a slot is replaced whole or not at all' to SPEC-ADDON-040. The spec text and its approval hash do not record this.; The spec does not state what a Media Import save does when removing the old picture fails, or that it prunes emptied directories. The code logs a warning and prunes through `remove_thumbnail_quietly` (backend/app/services/thumbnail.py:634-643), and tests cite SPEC-ADDON-040 for both.; The atomic publish also applies to subscription avatars, because `_save_subscription_avatar` shares `_download_thumbnail_sync` (service.py:574). The spec's touch points name only `_save_loft_thumbnail`. The behaviour is harmless: a failed avatar download now keeps the earlier avatar whole.

The spec does not state that a thumbnail download is atomic; item 5 says only that failure handling is unchanged (docs/specs/thumbnail-slot-ownership.md:155). The code publishes through `generating_file` (service.py:545), and test_loft_thumbnail.py:483 attributes 'a slot is replaced whole or not at all' to SPEC-ADDON-040.; The spec does not state that a Media Import save logs and continues when removing the old picture fails, or that it prunes emptied directories. `remove_thumbnail_quietly` does both (backend/app/services/thumbnail.py:634-643), and the path is reached from service.py:625-626.; If the row disappears during the download, `_save_loft_thumbnail` returns None and leaves the newly written slot file with no row (service.py:618-619). The spec does not describe this case. It needs a delete racing a download and is harmless to display.
